cases.purpose: On a disposable loop-mounted ext4 filesystem, verify that an immutable relative regular file cannot be unlinked by relative or absolute path, retains its exact bytes, and is cleared during teardown before it can be unlinked. The historical parity case is preserved separately.
cases.comparison: Each side asserts nonzero status and a nonempty diagnostic for both paths, exact retained bytes and entry, successful flag readback and cleanup; canonical observations are compared. Diagnostic wording differs between the Bash builtin and GNU unlink.
cases.script:
I=/tmp/unlink-immutable.img M=/tmp/unlink-immutable-mnt
mounted=0
cleanup() {
  local rc=$?
  trap - EXIT
  if (( mounted )); then
    cd /tmp/parity-case || rc=1
    /usr/bin/chattr -i "$M/imm" 2>/dev/null || { [[ ! -e $M/imm ]] || rc=1; }
    /usr/bin/umount "$M" || rc=1
  fi
  /usr/bin/rmdir "$M" 2>/dev/null || { [[ ! -d $M ]] || rc=1; }
  /usr/bin/rm -f "$I" || rc=1
  exit "$rc"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
/usr/bin/truncate -s 4M "$I" && /usr/sbin/mkfs.ext4 -q -F -O ^has_journal "$I" && /usr/bin/mkdir "$M" && /usr/bin/mount -o loop "$I" "$M" || { echo SETUP-FAILED >&2; exit 99; }
mounted=1
cd "$M" || exit 99
printf 'kept\n' > imm || exit 99
printf 'kept\n' > expected || exit 99
/usr/bin/chattr +i imm || { echo SETUP-FAILED-immutable >&2; exit 99; }
flags=$(/usr/bin/lsattr -d imm) || exit 99
[[ ${flags%% *} == *i* ]] || { echo SETUP-FAILED-flag >&2; exit 99; }
for path in imm "$PWD/imm"; do
  if unlink "$path" > /tmp/unlink-immutable.out 2> /tmp/unlink-immutable.err; then
    echo UNLINK-UNEXPECTED-SUCCESS >&2; exit 1
  fi
  [[ ! -s /tmp/unlink-immutable.out && -s /tmp/unlink-immutable.err && -f imm ]] || exit 1
  /usr/bin/cmp -s imm expected || exit 1
  echo denial-ok
done
/usr/bin/chattr -i imm || exit 1
flags=$(/usr/bin/lsattr -d imm) || exit 1
[[ ${flags%% *} != *i* ]] || exit 1
echo flag-cleared
unlink imm || exit 1
[[ ! -e imm && ! -L imm ]] || exit 1
echo cleared-unlink-ok
